Assuming an animal fat price of $0.76/kg, the MFSP of the HC via the HEFA-SPK pathway is estimated to be more than $19/gge (Table 12) for feedstocks from a 100-mile collection radius, simply due to the low volume of animal fat feedstocks, and cost is penalized by the economy of scale. Annual HC production is estimated to be one-fifth of 1 MMgge, so coupling with other waste oil feedstocks and increasing the collection radius would be recommended. Brown grease could be processed via the HEFA pathway to produce HC. Feedstock costs $426/ton ($0.47/kg) (Milbrandt and Badgett 2024). Unlike animal fats, the availability of brown grease is significant for both collection radii studied. With a lower feedstock brown grease price of $0.47/kg, the MFSP of the HC via the HEFA-SPK pathway is estimated at approximately $5.2/gge for feedstock collected from 50 miles (Table 13) and $3.6/gge for feedstocks from a 100-mile collection radius. The conversion cost without considering feedstock cost would be $3.3/gge and $1.8/gge, respectively. This means that HC’s minimum selling prices are still higher than that of the conventional jet fuel with brown grease, but the delta between the two is improved.
